messages.content: Contemplate on few lines of “Part four” (page 153) of this novel, “Majid: Wake up, Bibi. I am going to take both of you to the village. When Majeed came out of the house carrying Jamila, wrapped in a thin... quilt, a bewilderedRahima at his heels, the brilliant moonlight at first blinded him.” Even if Majeed was mostly depicted as a cunning and apathetic person throughout the narrative, do you find the same character traits in the mentioned lines? Was he trying to save Rahima and Jamila out of good-will (deontology) or his action was well-calculated (teleology)?Explain it. Include at least 10 single-word palindromes, each at least 5 characters long.

message.content:
In those lines, Majeed is not shown as openly apathetic; he is active, commanding, and physically present. He wakes Bibi, carries Jamila, and takes Rahima to the village. That movement can look protective, even if the thin quilt suggests only minimal comfort. So the same traits are still visible, but softened and turned inward: his cunning appears in control and decision; his apathy is masked by urgent action.

His motive, however, remains ambiguous. A deontological reading would say he saves them out of good-will or duty: they are vulnerable, it would be wrong to leave them, and he acts because he ought to, regardless of personal benefit. A teleological reading would say he acts because the consequences serve him: he avoids blame, danger, disorder, or loss, and preserves his position. Given that Majeed has mostly been portrayed as calculating and self-protecting, the teleological reading fits better: the rescue is a well-calculated move, a practical way to manage risk and control others, even if it momentarily resembles compassion.

The moonlight that blinds him deepens the ambiguity: it shows physical exposure, but it does not clarify his inner moral reason. Thus, the passage can be read as a rare humane impulse, yet the larger narrative pattern suggests a strategic act that looks like good-will while still serving his interests.

Palindromes: radar, level, kayak, rotor, civic, refer, reviver, rotator, deified, racecar.
